transcript.text: Can you describe your role and key responsibilities as Managing Partner in your family auto-parts business?

I've run our family's auto-parts business in Ludhiana for eight years. We have about 22 employees, and three supervisors report to me. Two years ago I added a second shift and our monthly output went up from 9,000 to 13,000 pieces. I also moved 70% of customer billing from cash to bank transfer. I'm applying to the one-year programme at IIM Lucknow because I learned everything on the job, and I'd like a framework for finance, costing and hiring.
What were the main challenges you faced in running day-to-day operations with a team of 22 employees and 3 supervisors?
transcript.anchor_quote: I've run our family's auto-parts business in Ludhiana for eight years. We have about 22 employees, and three supervisors report to me

transcript.text: I don't think the assumption that family businesses lack discipline is right in our case. We keep stock registers, and we pay on fixed dates. I'd like you to ask about specific problems.
You mentioned moving 70% of customer billing from cash to bank transfer. What motivated that change, and how did you manage the transition with your customers?
transcript.anchor_quote: I also moved 70% of customer billing from cash to bank transfer

transcript.text: Our business is built on trust and long-term relationships. We believe in quality and customer satisfaction, and our values have helped us grow steadily over the years.
How did you communicate these values of trust and quality to your customers during the shift to 70% bank transfer payments, and did you face any resistance?
transcript.anchor_quote: Our business is built on trust and long-term relationships

transcript.text: The second shift was my father's decision. I wasn't involved. I only managed the supervisors after he decided it.

You said your father decided to add the second shift and you managed the supervisors afterward. Can you describe how you handled the challenges or changes this second shift brought to your daily operations?
I can't share our profits, our customers' names or our bank loan details. They belong to the family and our partners, and I'd need their permission.

feedback.summary: The candidate has solid hands-on experience managing and scaling a family auto-parts business with about 22 employees, showing personal ownership in operations and implementing payment systems. However, there is limited articulation of challenges faced or specific problems solved, and minimal detail on the candidate's individual role in key decisions like adding a second shift. Responses lack concrete examples of personal judgment or learning from setbacks. The candidate is cautious about sharing sensitive details, which limits insight into business outcomes and peer contributions.
